marks.gloss_en: תניא נמי הכי: אין אומרים אהבת עולם אלא אהבה רבה
the baraita's tanna kama: one does not say 'An eternal love' but 'An abounding love'

דאמר רב חייא בר אשי: ... הוה מקדים וקא משי ידיה ובריך ומתני לן פרקין -- Rav recited the blessing before teaching the Sifra of his school; the redactor places this as the ground for Rava's ruling (that the Sifra teaching counts as 'talmud' is Steinsaltz's explanation, not the text's)
Rav Chiyya bar Ashi: many times I stood before Rav to learn our chapter in the Sifra of Rav's school; he would first wash his hands, recite the blessing, and then teach us our chapter
לימא: יוצר אור ובורא נוגה! -- why not say 'creates brightness' and avoid the word darkness?

אלא אמר רבא: כדי להזכיר מדת יום בלילה ומדת לילה ביום -- 'creates darkness' is kept so that night's attribute is mentioned by day (= p_rava_purpose_choshech); the first answer, כדכתיב קאמרינן (11b.3), was rejected at 11b.4 -- see obj_ela_meata
Rava: 'creates darkness' is said in order to mention the attribute of night by day (and the attribute of day at night)

אלא מעתה: עושה שלום ובורא רע -- מי קא אמרינן כדכתיב?! אלא כתיב רע וקרינן הכל לישנא מעליא; הכא נמי לימא נוגה לישנא מעליא -- the same verse's 'creates evil' is already NOT said as written, so 'as written' cannot be the reason; unanswered, and the answer is abandoned at אלא (11b.5)
the verse's own continuation, 'Who makes peace and creates evil', is NOT said as written: 'evil' is written and 'all things' is said, a refined expression
בשלמא מדת לילה ביום כדאמרינן יוצר אור ובורא חשך, אלא מדת יום בלילה היכי משכחת לה? -- granted night's attribute is mentioned by day; where is day's attribute mentioned at night?
אמר אביי: גולל אור מפני חשך וחשך מפני אור (= p_golel_or)
Abaye: the attribute of day is mentioned at night in the words 'rolling away light before darkness and darkness before light'
הלכך לימרינהו לכולהו -- therefore let us say them all
therefore let us say them all
R' Oshaya (via R' Yaakov): the first blessing is 'Who forms light and creates darkness' (Isa 45:7)
the stam's first answer: we say 'creates darkness' because that is how the verse is written
the second blessing before the Shema is 'An abounding love' (ahava rabba)
one who rose early to study: before he has read the Shema he must recite the blessing over Torah
for Scripture one must recite the blessing
R' Elazar: for midrash (as for Scripture) one must recite the blessing
R' Yochanan: for mishnah too one must recite the blessing
Rava: for talmud too one must recite the blessing (the text prints לחזור ולברך in parentheses and לברך in brackets)
Shmuel (via Rav Yehuda): the blessing over Torah is '...Who sanctified us with His commandments and commanded us to engage in words of Torah'
R' Yochanan closes it thus: 'make the words of Your Torah sweet in our mouths... Blessed are You, Lord, Who teaches Torah to His people Israel'
Rav Hamnuna: '...Who chose us from all the peoples and gave us His Torah. Blessed are You, Lord, Giver of the Torah'
זאת אומרת: from ברכו ברכה אחת -- a single blessing sufficed -- it follows that the blessings do not impede one another
Reish Lakish (as R' Zerika reports in R' Ami's name): the one blessing is 'Who forms light'

אי אמרת בשלמא יוצר אור הוו אמרי, היינו דברכות אין מעכבות זו את זו, דלא קא אמרי אהבה רבה; אלא אי אמרת אהבה רבה הוו אמרי, מאי ברכות אין מעכבות זו את זו? דלמא האי דלא אמרי יוצר אור משום דלא מטא זמן יוצר אור, וכי מטא זמן יוצר אור הוו אמרי -- only if the watch said יוצר אור does 'not impeding' follow from their omitting אהבה רבה; had they said אהבה רבה, omitting יוצר אור could be because its time had not come

mishnah Tamid: the appointed one told the watch to say one blessing; they blessed, read the Ten Commandments and the three Shema paragraphs, and blessed the people with three blessings (True and Firm, Avoda, the priestly blessing); on Shabbat one blessing is added for the outgoing watch
Shmuel: the one blessing is 'An abounding love'
